20397b96d8cb8c1ee915292f80346562294bddc0.summary: This is a webinar listing from Kaspersky, announcing a talk on the Fin7 group. It says Fin7 continued after the 2018 arrests of its leaders, extended its operations to more groups, and still aims to steal financial assets. The page contains no technical findings of its own, and most of it is channel and company boilerplate, so it is not a threat report.

audit_history.note: summary: The text says only "Europol and the DoJ" announced the arrests. It never says "US", so "US DoJ" adds detail the text doesn't give.

audit.note: summary: The summary drops the text's hedges and misstates the content. The text says that after the 2018 arrests it was believed the group would cease activity

20676725f96ecb865989fb60464f45ba38147dde.summary: FireEye describes an SSH brute-force campaign from an address block registered to Hee Thai Limited, running from November 2014. It targets root accounts on servers and network devices to install XOR.DDoS, a Linux DDoS bot with a rootkit. An on-demand build system compiles tailored malware per victim kernel, defeating hash-based detection. The report describes two variants, persistence behaviour and defensive advice.

20baf490bcac32036585fda02e82e70a312212dd.summary: A BleepingComputer article from July 2022 reports that at least two ransomware operations and a data extortion gang added search functions to their leak sites, making stolen victim data easier to find. The named groups are ALPHV/BlackCat, LockBit and Karakurt. The article says it is unclear whether searchable stolen data is a successful tactic, and that more threat actors are likely to adopt it.

actors.q: Last week, the ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware operation announced that they created a searchable database
Towards the end of last week, BleepingComputer noticed that LockBit offered a redesigned version of their data leak site
Another leak site that has implemented a search function is the one published by the Karakurt data extortion gang.

sectors.q: data allegedly stolen in an attack at a hotel and spa in Oregon

dates.q: The gang already tried this strategy in mid-June
dates.what: ALPHV/BlackCat earlier created a searchable site with data allegedly stolen in an attack at a hotel and spa in Oregon

techniques.v: search function on the leak site
techniques.q: The new tactic consists in adding a search function on the leak site to make it easier to find victims or even specific details.

techniques.v: puts pressure on the victim to pay the ransom
techniques.q: This is a step forward in the extortion business as it puts pressure on the victim to pay the ransom and have the data removed

figures.q: At least two ransomware operations and a data extortion gang have adopted the strategy recently

hedges: The results may not have the best accuracy but it is still an evolution of the cybercriminal's extortion strategy.
data allegedly stolen in an attack at a hotel and spa in Oregon
BlackCat ransomware operators claim that they do this to make it easier for other cybercriminals to find passwords or confidential information about companies.
LockBit's search is not as advanced as the variant touted by BlackCat, and it is limited to only finding victims by name.
BleepingComputer's attempts to use the option showed that it did not work properly, though.
It is unclear if making stolen data searchable is a successful tactic but with multiple extortionist gangs adopting it, the option seems to be an attractive one.
more threat actors are likely to do the same
